evidence.observation: The single panel-config resolution point. Every field is produced by env()/envInt()/envBool() with a hard-coded literal fallback, which establishes the two lower precedence layers: panel config (process.env, populated by dotenv) wins over the default literal. loadPanelConfig() reads process.env at call time, so config-vs-default conflicts are directly observable without restarting the process.

The config/default conflict rule in concrete form: an env value that is undefined, empty string, or non-finite does NOT win over the default; it falls through to the fallback. Same shape in env() (line 6-8, ?? fallback) and envBool() (line 37-41, only 'true'/'1' count). This is the tie-break when config is present-but-degenerate.

Declares the config surface. The knowledge block (lines 23-24) documents the top precedence layer: 'serviceId 按请求 instanceId 注入' — the per-request instance id is injected as the Knowledge Service serviceId, overriding/selecting the instance the panel talks to, while baseUrl/authToken/timeoutMs come from panel config.

The config-over-default primitive: `process.env[key] ?? fallback`. Independent of envInt/envBool, it proves the middle layer (config) beats the lowest layer (default) for string fields such as HOST, KNOWLEDGE_SERVICE_URL and METADATA_INSTANCES_CONFIG.

The explicit-request-input layer for instances: the per-request instanceId (from the x-tdai-service-id header) is looked up in the registry. A miss throws InstanceRegistryError(400, 'INVALID_INSTANCE') — request input is never silently reconciled with a default instance, so an unknown request id outranks the fallback instead of degrading to it.

Default-layer fallback for instance config: when a configured entry has no proxy_endpoint the field is omitted from the public payload (not set to explicit undefined), documented as the frontend falling back to gateway_endpoint via `??`. So explicit config (proxy_endpoint present) beats the gateway_endpoint default, and api_key never leaves the process.

claims.claim: MemoryPanel instance/panel configuration resolves conflicts in the order explicit request input > panel config > default. Config (process.env, loaded by dotenv) overrides the hard-coded fallback literals in loadPanelConfig, and a per-request x-tdai-service-id selects the configured instance (and is injected as the knowledge serviceId) rather than being merged with a default.

When panel config and default conflict, a present-but-degenerate config value does not win: env() falls back via `??`, envInt() rejects undefined/empty/non-finite and returns the fallback, and envBool() accepts only 'true'/'1'. Only a well-formed env value outranks the default.

When explicit request input and instance config conflict, the request wins: resolve() returns the requested entry's configured gateway_endpoint/api_key, and an instance id absent from config is rejected with InstanceRegistryError code 400 'INVALID_INSTANCE' instead of falling back to any default instance.

At the default layer inside instance config, an absent proxy_endpoint falls back to gateway_endpoint: listPublic() omits the field entirely so the consumer's `??` yields gateway_endpoint, while an explicitly configured proxy_endpoint wins; api_key is never exposed in the public listing.

conclusion: The precedence contract for MemoryPanel instance/panel configuration is explicit request input > panel config > default, verified executably against the repository's real modules. In an intentional three-way conflict: (1) a per-request instance id (x-tdai-service-id) selects the configured InstanceEntry and is injected as the knowledge serviceId, and an unknown id is hard-rejected (400 INVALID_INSTANCE) with no default fallback; (2) process.env values consumed by loadPanelConfig (PORT=9000 vs default 8123, KNOWLEDGE_TIMEOUT_MS=7777 vs 15000, LOG_LEVEL=debug vs info) beat the hard-coded defaults, while empty/non-numeric/out-of-set config values fall back to the default; (3) default-layer fallbacks apply only when neither of the higher layers supplies a value, with proxy_endpoint falling back to gateway_endpoint. All 23 demo assertions passed.
